What is the difference between a choropleth and an isoline map?
options: Choropleths use coloured/shaded areas to show data values per region (e.g. population density by county); isoline maps use lines connecting points of equal value (e.g. contours, isobars).

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.
The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.
